### Discipleship sweep: the event's organisation, and the switch, per organisation (#812, #819)

- Rule 3 trusted the RSVP row's own `siteID` as its organisation test. That column is a COPY of the event's organisation, made once by `calendar/rsvp.php`; rules 1 and 2 ask the event itself (`ev.siteID = p.siteID`). Rule 3 now does too. Nothing else in the join crosses organisations: the enrolment is reached through the pathway, the step through its pathway, the pathway by `p.siteID = ?`. None of the three rules asks whether the person is still a member of the organisation; that is a different question and was left alone.
- `Discipleship::isEnabledFor($siteId)` ASKS `AppRegistry::isEnabledForSite('discipleship', $siteId)` — own row, else installation-wide; exactly `'1'`/`'true'` is on; no row is off — so there is one rule. It was a copy at first; X18i/X18j drove the real job over ten stored values and over no row with the copy and with the call, and both gave the same answers. `Discipleship::isEnabled()` stays for pages, which are about their own organisation.
- Round-1 lesson: the first tests turned the switch on only through an organisation's OWN row, a state no page can produce; a switch that ignored the installation-wide row — the only row Admin, Apps writes — passed them all. The ordinary state (installation-wide on, no own rows) is X18g. And the outcome the job RECORDS (`tblScheduledJobRun.lastOutcome`, which the Check page reads) was pinned by nothing; each run now deletes the job's record first and reads it back.
- Testing trap: to make a setting MISSING, do not rename it to `discipleship.enabled.<x>` — setting names are a dotted tree, so that turns the key into a branch, and `Settings::get()` then returns an array (`isEnabled()` warned "Array to string conversion").
- Testing trap found by planting: a sweep that completes EVERY step of a pathway also marks the enrolment `completed`, and the sweep only reads `active` enrolments, so a fixture reused across arrangements must put the enrolment back to `active` as well as deleting the progress rows — otherwise a later check fails for the wrong reason.
- To find progress rows already written across organisations (none exist on any installation, since none is live; nothing deletes them):
  ```sql
  SELECT `pr`.`progressID`, `pr`.`siteID` AS `pathwayOrganisation`, `ev`.`siteID` AS `eventOrganisation`,
         `pr`.`userID`, `pr`.`stepID`, `pr`.`autoRef`, `pr`.`completedAt`, `pr`.`revokedAt`
  FROM `tblPathwayProgress` `pr`
  JOIN `tblEvents` `ev` ON `ev`.`eventID` = CAST(SUBSTRING(`pr`.`autoRef`, 6) AS UNSIGNED)
  WHERE `pr`.`source` = 'auto' AND `pr`.`autoRef` LIKE 'rsvp:%' AND `ev`.`siteID` <> `pr`.`siteID`;
  ```
  It joins on the event the row's own evidence names (`autoRef`), not on the step's current event, because a step's event can be edited after the row was written.
- Tests: X18b-X18l of `tools/time-zones-selftest.php` (EXPECTED_CHECKS 175 → 186).

**Review: three rounds by fresh Claude agents; round 3 CLEAN** (protected arm — the sweep writes permanent progress rows). Rounds 1 and 2 found only tests that could not fail (the ordinary installation-wide switch state, the recorded outcome, the printed counts); the portal code was correct in every state driven on MySQL 8.0.36 and MariaDB 11.4. Codex has NOT reviewed it. Left on #824 (departed members still count), #825, #827.

### A cache must know what it is a cache OF (#799)

`tblContentTranslation` was keyed on (table, row, field, target language). That
says WHICH piece, never WHAT IT SAYS, so the key matched after the words had
changed and the cache went on answering. `Translation::sourceFingerprint()`
(SHA-256 of the exact text `translate()` was given — the text sent to the
provider, which the one caller reads with `ContentTranslation::readSourceText()`)
is computed ONCE in `translate()` and used for both the look-up and the store,
so the two cannot fingerprint different things. `lookupCached()` compares it in
the statement (`AND sourceHash = ?`), so a row made from other words is never
read.

Four things worth keeping:

- **Fingerprint, not delete-on-save.** Deleting rows in every editor would need
  every page and API that can change those words to remember, and the first
  that forgot would bring the fault back invisibly. The fingerprint is checked
  at the one place a translation is served.
- **The update clause of the upsert must write the fingerprint too.** A
  re-translation is a DUPLICATE of the old row, so if `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`
  left `sourceHash` alone the row would carry the old words' fingerprint, never
  match again, and every press after an edit would be a paid request for ever.
  Check E3-06 exists for exactly that.
- **NULL is stale, not fresh.** Rows from before migration 256 have no
  fingerprint and `NULL = ?` never matches. Backfilling from each source's
  current words was rejected because it would stamp every old translation as
  matching its original whether or not the original had been edited — the
  fault written into the data. The cost is one more paid request per piece and
  language, and a press refused (rather than served) while a month's limit is
  reached.
- **Not tidied before fingerprinting.** A translation is of exactly these
  words; deciding which edits "do not count" would mean the one that matters
  gets served wrong.

**And a second fault on the same line:** `persist()`'s `bind_param` types were
`'sissssisi'` (and `'sissssis'` before `e7afab2`), binding the PROVIDER as `i`,
so every row since `8625b9e` stored `0`. Measured on MySQL 8.0.36 by binding
`'libre'` with the original types. Nothing reads the column, which is why it
survived; E3-05c pins it now. **Count a types string against its values, one
per argument, whenever a statement gains a column** — `e7afab2` added one and
kept the shape.

What the fix does NOT do, said plainly: a translation of an edited original is
not deleted, only never shown again and replaced on the next request in that
language; a translation of a DELETED original is never shown (it can only be
asked for through the original, which then answers "not found") and is never
removed. Two presses of an edited piece at the same moment both pay, as two
presses of a new piece always have (#766).

Tests: section E3 of `tools/content-translation-selftest.php` (real HTTP, real
MySQL, the stub provider). Plants and their results are in the commit message.

**Review: protected arm (money), two rounds by fresh Claude agents standing in for Codex; round 2 CLEAN.** Round 1 found the engine, migration and tests sound (seven builder plants plus five of its own, each caught) and ONE untrue sentence: `help/translations.php` still said anything already translated keeps working, which the admin page and `api-spec.json` had been corrected for in the same package. **A correction applied to two of the three places a claim lives is the recurring shape** — search for the sentence, not the file you remember it in. Still true and stated rather than fixed: "pieces already translated from their current words keep working" does not hold for a copy made before migration 256, which has no fingerprint; no installation exists, so nothing is affected. Codex has NOT reviewed it.

### Content translation follows its own app switch (#792, D-075)

`AppRegistry::API_FOLDER_APPS['translation']` was `null` ("belongs to the
portal") from e54fa7f. The app definition `_core/apps/translation.php` has named
`translation.enabled` as its switch since 8625b9e (#285), so the switch existed;
only the router's app gate did not ask it. Effects of `null`, now gone: a press
reached `ApiAuth::requireWrite()` and had its form token replaced before the
handler refused it, and the answer used the handler's own words rather than the
router's.

- **`ContentTranslation::isSwitchedOn()` is the one question**, asked by
  `translate-control.php`, `translation/api/content.php` and
  `account/translation.php`. It requires BOTH readings: `AppRegistry::isEnabled()`
  (the router's, `'1'` or `'true'`) AND the stored value being exactly `'1'`
  (the engine's, in the pinned `Translation.php`). Asking only the router would
  draw a button that 503s on a hand-written `'true'`.
- **The handler's own switch test is reached through the router in ONE case
  only:** a switch stored by hand as `'true'`, which the router counts as on and
  `isSwitchedOn()` as off — refused there, after the form token was replaced,
  with nothing sent or charged. No fixture stores `'true'`, so that branch and
  the `=== '1'` half of `isSwitchedOn()` are guarded by no test (round 1 planted
  it out and everything stayed green). Round 1 caught an earlier version of
  this note, and of the handler's comment, saying it was unreachable.
- **The account page stays open while the app is off**, because it is where a
  member withdraws permission; it shows `#translation-switched-off`.
- **The admin page is closed by the router while the app is off**, as it always
  was (`admin/translation` is the app's `route`). Both it and Admin → Apps need
  a global administrator, so whoever can untick its box can switch it back on.
- No database change: `translation.enabled` was already seeded `'0'`, like
  sms, payments, giving, zoom and transcription.
- **The earlier section "What the tests cannot do, said once here as well"
  (#485) is now out of date on ORDER**: it says the handler asks first. Since
  #792 the router asks first. The handler's switch test is reached over HTTP
  only for a hand-written `'true'`, and the engine's is not reached over HTTP at
  all, because the handler applies the same exact-`'1'` test and refuses first.
  (Round 1 of the check caught an earlier draft of this note saying neither was
  reachable.)

### A regular expression that runs out of stack answers "not found" (#792)

`sm_dashboardAlert()` in `tools/db-strict-mode-selftest.php` used
`(?:(?!<div class="alert ).)*` between an alert's heading and its last line.
That walks to the end of the page and back; PCRE's JIT stack ran out once the
page after the alert exceeded about 20-30 KB (measured on the real page: 20,000
bytes matched, 30,000 did not), and `preg_match()` returned `false`, which the
`!== 1 → return null` read as "no alert". The alert markup and the extractor
both date from 04eb374 and never changed; the dashboard source grew from 39 KB
(21a8935) to 57 KB (0e15afd). **Two lessons:** a tempered greedy token over a
whole page has a size limit nobody sees; and `preg_match() !== 1` treats an
ERROR as "absent", which makes a "shows no X" check pass on any page. The same
`=== 1 ? … : ''` shape with tempered tokens is in `access-pages-selftest.php`,
`gdpr-coverage-selftest.php`, `go-live-button-selftest.php` and
`time-zones-selftest.php` — each bounded by one element, so lower risk, but not
checked.

**Review: protected arm (money), two rounds by fresh Claude agents standing in for Codex.** Round 1 found the behaviour right and two untrue comments (the handler's switch test "can never be the one that says no", false for a hand-written `'true'`; and part P "would have passed whatever the dashboard drew", an overstatement) plus an untrue Admin → Apps sentence about who chooses the translation company. Round 2 found the code and spec fixes true and one draft note still untrue, which was corrected without a further round because it is documentation. Codex has NOT reviewed it. Left open: #829, #831.

### The top bar must fit with every app on (#822)

- **The fault needs a crowded bar, which is why nothing found it.** Every earlier layout audit
  ran signed out, or as an account with few apps. A test world must be built to the WORST
  case on purpose — every app on, a long organisation name, long personal names — or a
  layout check of shared furniture proves nothing about it. `tools/top-bar-selftest.php`
  asserts that premise first (the Apps menu holds at least 30 entries).
- **Three CSS facts that each caused a fault here:**
  1. A flex item will not shrink below its content unless it is given `min-width: 0`, and
     Bootstrap's `.navbar-brand` is `white-space: nowrap`. Together they let one long name
     widen the page.
  2. Bootstrap utilities are `!important`. `bottom-0` beat the inline `style.bottom` that
     pwa-install.js set, so its "lift above the cookie banner" never ran — invisible because
     the two notices rarely show together.
  3. `backdrop-filter` creates a stacking context. With no z-index the bar's own dropdowns
     could rise no higher than the bar, which sat beneath any positioned element later in the
     page. It is now `position: relative; z-index: 1020` (Bootstrap's sticky-bar level),
     below the notices (1080) and dialogs (1055).
- **A grid menu needs its display rule restated.** Bootstrap's `.dropdown-menu.show` and the
  portal's no-JavaScript hover rule both say `display: block`; the Apps menu needs `grid`, so
  its rules carry `.navbar` in the selector to win regardless of order.
- **`minmax(13rem, 1fr)` is not enough on a phone**: the column must also be capped at the
  menu's width — `minmax(min(13rem, 100%), 1fr)` — and the entries allowed to wrap
  (`white-space: normal`), or one long app name pushes the menu off a 320px screen.
- **Keyboard:** Bootstrap's arrow keys move through the entries in document order, so in a
  four-column grid ArrowDown moves to the entry on the RIGHT. Measured working (Enter opens,
  arrows move, Escape closes and returns focus); the reading order is alphabetical either way.
- **A no-JavaScript fallback must be scoped to no-JavaScript.** portal.css's section 12 said
  "when JS is unavailable" and applied always; the comment described an intent the selector did not
  implement. The mark is `data-portal-menus` on `<html>`, set by portal.js only once
  `bootstrap.Dropdown` exists, and looked for again at the page's `load` event because the local
  fallback copy is added after the CDN fails and may arrive late. **Mark the thing the fallback
  depends on, not a neighbour of it:** round 1 set `data-portal-js` from header.php's inline head
  script, which proves that inline scripts run — not that Bootstrap arrived — so with Bootstrap
  blocked the fallback switched itself off and nothing on the bar could be opened (round 2,
  measured in Edge; round 3 measured the fix with Bootstrap normal, blocked, and the CDN failing
  with the local copy present).
- **Check every instance of the control, not two of them.** Round 1's test checked "focus alone
  shows nothing" on Apps and Admin and "a resting pointer opens nothing" on Apps only, so a rule
  opening the account menu on focus passed with exit 0; it now walks every visible
  `[data-bs-toggle="dropdown"]` on the bar.
- **Review: presentation arm, three rounds by fresh Claude agents standing in for Codex; round 3
  CLEAN.** Codex has NOT reviewed it.
- **A test that checks its own clean-up must not read the clean-up's list.** The put-back check
  compares against the three snapshots separately; comparing against `$putBack` (the list the
  restore uses) passed when a value was dropped from it — planted.
- **How the self-test plants:** `TOP_BAR_SELFTEST_WEB` serves another copy of `web/`, so a
  fault is planted in a scratch copy and never in the working tree.

### A search that could not run must never answer the question (#829)
`preg_match()` returns `false`, `preg_match_all()` `false`, `preg_replace()`
`null` and `preg_split()` `false` when PCRE cannot finish — the JIT stack, the
backtracking limit, or bad UTF-8 under `/u`. Every comparison this repository's
tests habitually write (`=== 1`, `!== 1`, `> 0`, `(string)`, `(array)`, `?: []`)
turns that into "absent". So a check that asks for ABSENCE is the one that goes
green on a page it never read, and it gets likelier as pages grow, because the
pages grow and the tests do not. The four tests named in #829 wrap every such call
(`ap_`, `gc_`, `glb_`, `tz_` prefixes); the wrapper records a red check first and
then throws, because a bare uncaught exception is a crash with a label. Deliberately
left raw: the router each HTTP test writes out for its web server (another process;
it searches a short request path with anchored patterns) and, in the go-live test,
`glb_stopWorkers()`, which the shutdown clean-up calls — a throw there would leave the
clean-up half done, and it reads single lines of `ps` output with an anchored pattern
that has no repeated group. **Not swept:** the other self-tests in `tools/`; the same
shape almost certainly exists there (one instance: `content-translation-selftest.php`
uses `(string) preg_replace('/\s+/u', …)`, where `/u` fails on invalid UTF-8).

### The two readers of `translation.enabled` (#831)
`AppRegistry::isEnabled()` accepts `'1'` and `'true'`; the pinned engine accepts
only `'1'`. `ContentTranslation::isSwitchedOn()` asks both, and section E2 of the
content-translation test is now what fails if it stops. What the test still cannot
plant without editing the pinned engine: the engine itself accepting `'true'`. The
"nothing sent / nothing counted" checks were proved able to fail with a plant that
loosens `isSwitchedOn()` AND hands the engine `'1'`, and E2-08 proves the stub log
and the usage row really do move on the same press once the switch says `'1'`.

**Review: tooling arm (tests only), one round by a fresh Claude agent standing in for Codex: CLEAN.** It re-ran all five tests old and new (counts unchanged except content-translation +13), confirmed every wrapper passes arguments, flags and the match array straight through, re-planted every E2 fault, killed content-translation inside E2 and found the settings put back, and repeated the starvation proof. It corrected one count in these notes (six, not five). Codex has NOT reviewed it. The rest of `tools/` is #837.

### An optional ceiling on registration retention (#816)

- `Portal\Core\RegistrationRetention` is the ONE reader and writer of `events.registrationRetentionDays` and `events.registrationRetentionMaxDays`. Two save-time gates (period above ceiling refused; ceiling below a held period refused and named) keep every period <= the ceiling by construction; the job does not cap (D-074 following D-032). Both gates re-read the ceiling `FOR UPDATE` inside the transaction that writes, and both savers lock the SAME row (the installation's ceiling row). Measured by section I of `tools/registration-retention-selftest.php`: a second connection holds that row; the save from a second process was still waiting after 2.5 s, and after commit it judged the new ceiling and refused. With ` FOR UPDATE` planted out, it did not wait and stored 25 days under a ceiling of 10.
- Gates judge only what CHANGED (#687): an untouched Save over a period above the ceiling passes.
- **No portal page or API writes `tblEvents.registrationRetentionDays`.** Established with `git grep -n "registrationRetentionDays" -- web` (7 November 2026): `calendar/manage/series-repattern.php` names it only to SKIP it, `events/api/detail.php` only reads it; section G of the test posts the field to `/api/events/create` and `/api/events/update` and finds the column still NULL. So an event's own period meets only gate 2. If a page is ever given a box for it, it must ask the class.
- The installation's period and ceiling are written only by a global administrator, re-checked inside `saveInstallation()`.
- Window between files landing and "Run migrations": the general editor already refuses the keys while the page's two addresses are not yet seeded, so the installation's period cannot be changed in that window (the portal is closed for the upgrade then anyway, `Maintenance::isActive()`).
- Test lesson worth keeping: the first version of section B posted to `/settings/save` without `settingKey`, which that handler requires before anything else, so every "refused" check passed for the wrong reason — plant P4 (the lock removed) stayed GREEN and exposed it. B0 now proves the same request shape changes an ordinary row. Also: `null ?? 'no row'` answers 'no row', so a check that a value IS null must use `array_key_exists`.
- **The test drives the REAL clear-out** over HTTP (`/cron/retention-sweep`) against registrations: an empty or non-numeric stored period keeps a 150-day-old registration (the pre-#816 reading), negative or missing reads as 90 days, a period above the ceiling (planted by SQL) is obeyed rather than capped, and `events.registrationRetentionRun` stored as `True` or ` true` keeps the job OFF while no row at all means ON — `RegistrationRetention::clearOutRunsForSite()` is the ONE reader of that switch. Round 1 found the first three and the reverse race (a lower ceiling saved while an organisation's raise is in flight) guarded by NOTHING; each now has a plant. **When a design promises 'the job keeps it longer', drive the job: a class-level test cannot see the job ignoring the class.**
- **A raised ceiling is refused too while a period above it exists** (D-032's rule). Round 1 briefly allowed raising — reverted in round 2, because D-074 says follow D-032 unless a measured fact makes it unworkable, and the case is reachable only by hand-written SQL. Removing the ceiling is always allowed and is the way out.

**Review: protected arm (personal data), three rounds by fresh Claude agents standing in for Codex; round 3 CLEAN.** 14 plants in the test, each red. Codex has NOT reviewed it. Left open: #835, #836, #840.

### A member's own claims (#834)

- The list is ONE read-only query in `web/_apps/expenses/submit/index.php`, scoped by `siteID = Site::id()` AND
  `userID = $_SESSION['user_id']`, ordered `createdAt DESC, claimID DESC` (the index
  `idx_claims_site_user_created` is exactly that). Both scopes are pinned by part P of
  `tools/access-pages-selftest.php`: planted out, removing the user condition turned P1, P2, P4-P8, P10 red;
  removing the organisation condition turned P1, P3, P6-P8 red; ordering by claim number instead of submitted time
  turned P1, P4-P7 red. The fixture gives "newest submitted" and "highest number" different orders on purpose.
- No Withdraw/Change button in the list, deliberately: that decision needs the approval count and belongs to
  `ExpenseRules::whyNotEditable()`, which the claim's page already asks (#651). A second place drawing those buttons
  is the drift the rule exists to prevent.
- A failed read says "could not be read just now" and records the exception; it never says "no claims yet", which
  would invite a duplicate claim. That branch is exercised by no automatic test; round 1 broke a column by hand to confirm it.
- The status-badge colours are a second copy of `expenses/view/index.php`'s `match` (comment in both says change
  together). Presentation only.
- **Round 1 found two checks that could not fail.** The error-row check filtered by `userID`, and `Logger::exception()` records no user — so the page's own errors were invisible to it (now P12: rows for organisations A and B above a mark taken at the start of part P). And nothing guarded the page-number validation: a bare `(int)` passed every check while `?page=0`, `-1`, `abc` or an empty value made the list say "could not be read" (now P11). **A check filtered on a column the writer never fills is a clause that cannot fail.**
- **How it was found:** #834 began as "check one help sentence" (#822's Found list). Checking it showed no page listed a member's claims and `ExpenseMailer` sends the claimant nothing on `submitted`, so a pending claim could not be reached at all (#841 is the e-mail). The dashboard card's comment asserted the opposite.

**Review: protected arm (a member's financial claims), two rounds by fresh Claude agents standing in for Codex; round 2's one finding was a check number in a test comment, corrected as documentation.** Codex has NOT reviewed it. Also found: #842 (two self-tests clash on one database).

### Locked settings, and a test that empties a shared table (#836, #842)

**A refusal list kept in three places goes out of step one path at a time.**
The general settings editor refuses keys that have their own page on three
paths — change, add (both in `settings/save.php`) and delete (in
`settings/index.php`). #502 found the delete missing two keys; #836 found it
missing `transcription.retentionDays` (#722 added the refusal to change and add
only). The ONE list is the set of `public static function …LockedInGeneralEditor()`
methods in `web/_core`; `tools/settings-locks-selftest.php` reads that set with
PHP's tokeniser, requires every method to be asked on every path (section S),
and drives the delete, change and add over HTTP for every key any method locks (section B).
A new lock method added to the save handler and not the delete now goes red
there without anybody remembering to add a case. The three paths still carry
one block per method rather than one loop, because existing tests pin those
blocks' exact text (capabilities-selftest, gdpr-coverage-selftest and
registration-retention-selftest at least); collapsing them into a loop is possible but means rewriting those
pins together.

**A test that empties a shared table breaks the NEXT test, not itself.**
`expense-edit-selftest.php` ran `DELETE FROM tblSites WHERE 1=1`; it passed,
and `page-scripts-selftest.php` run next on the same database failed 17 of 88
(it seeded into `MIN(siteID)`, by then the other test's leftover 916801, while
the portal served organisation 1). Delete by your own numbers; and seed into
what the portal will serve, asked of the portal's own rule.

**Three check rounds found only tests that could not fail, and each is the same shape:** the expense-edit test counted the rows it must not touch AFTER its own clean-up had already emptied them; the giving-records hold check saved the value already stored, so a silently dropped save passed; and the settings-locks header claimed other tests drove change and add for `transcription.retentionDays` when no file in `tools/` posted that key at all. **A check that compares before with after must take 'before' before anything can change it, and a check that an action was accepted must make the action change something.**

**Review: protected arm (retention settings), three rounds by fresh Claude agents standing in for Codex; every finding was in tests (D-064); round 3 CLEAN.** Codex has NOT reviewed it. Left open: #845, #846. The new test is wired into the runner and workflow in a following commit, because those two files carry another package's uncommitted changes.

### A focus ring, phone widths, and `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (#832, #833)

- **`overflow-wrap: anywhere` is not a stronger `break-word`; it changes layout.** Both break a word that
  would overflow its line, but `anywhere` also lets those breaks count towards an element's min-content
  width (CSS Text 3). The property is inherited, so every flex item inside the cell could then shrink below
  its own one-word label: a button beside a `width: 100%` input took its share of the negative free space
  and split "Ignore". `break-word` leaves min-content alone. Use `anywhere` only where shrinking below a
  word is the point.
- **`min-width: 0` does nothing on a column flex item's width.** On a phone `.portal-data-row` is
  `flex-direction: column`, where a flex item's automatic minimum applies to the main axis (its height).
  A comment crediting `min-width: 0` with letting the cell give way was untrue and the line is gone.
- **A page list is only measured if it is drawn.** The test seeded one session and two members, so neither
  page's pagination ever appeared and both could be wider than a phone unseen. It now seeds 200 of each,
  and reads /admin/users?page=4, because the widest pagination is on a MIDDLE page.
- **The contrast figure for "the lowest" must name what it is measured against.** The comment named the
  highlighted current-page entry; the figures were for `--portal-surface-hover`, the background Bootstrap
  gives a FOCUSED outline button (`.btn:focus-visible` paints `--bs-btn-hover-bg`).
- **Specificity of `:is()` is its most specific argument.** `[tabindex]` in the list is what makes the rule
  (0,3,0) and lets it beat `.btn.show:focus-visible`; without it the rule is (0,2,1).
- **Work out a contrast from the value that APPLIES, after the cascade.** A round-2 correction gave the
  dark-theme figure for the highlighted entry as "about 14.1 to 14.9:1", computed from a colour-mixed
  `--portal-primary-subtle` in an `@supports` block that the later plain dark block overrides. The value
  that applies is `#1f2347`, giving 12.56:1. Round 3 caught it; the same cascade is #852's third item.

### Three older layout faults (#852)

- **Print one marker per gap, not one per position.** The page lists placed "…" at fixed positions (page
  4 and page N-3; page 3 and page N-2). Near either end of a long list every page between the two is hidden
  as well, and the two "…" printed side by side; on a middle page they fell in separate gaps and looked
  right, which is why it went unnoticed. Tracking whether the last thing printed was already a "…" is
  right whatever the window. The same loop had been copied onto
  four more pages; the audit check now refuses the shape anywhere.
- **A check's premise must not be measured from the faulty output.** The first ellipsis check required at
  least eight entries, a count taken from the list WITH the duplicate; the correct page 1 of /admin/users
  has seven, so the fix failed its own check. And page 1 has ONE gap, so a loop that drops the SECOND
  "…" passes there: the check also reads a page from the middle of each list, and counts page numbers that
  jump with no "…" between them. It names those middle pages exactly — asking for two gaps on any address
  with `page=` went red on users' page 4, whose list has one.
- **A later rule of equal weight replaces an earlier one entirely.** `.alert { padding: … }` in portal.css
  loads after Bootstrap, so it also replaced `.alert-dismissible { padding-right: 3rem }`. Put back as
  `padding-inline-end`, because Bootstrap's right-to-left build puts the X on the left.
- **Letting text wrap changes how a flex row shares its width.** A `nowrap` badge made its half of the row
  as wide as the badge, so only the title shrank. Once badges could wrap, a badge alone in a row's aside
  shrank too and split over two lines; the aside keeps `nowrap`. And `word-break: break-word` inherited
  from a `.text-break` cell would split a badge's word once it may wrap, so the badge resets it.

### Show on the public website, for events (#493, package P1)

`EventVisibility::where()` in "website" mode is still the ONE rule for who may see an event on the
public website; `Portal\Core\PublicWebsite` decides the three things around it (who may change the
switch, whether a posted change is allowed, and which copied-in rule an organisation is held to). Four
lessons from its checking, each a shape worth recognising elsewhere.

- **A new parameter with a STRICTER default narrows every caller that omits it — tests included.**
  `where()` gained `$copiedRule`, defaulting to "one tick per event". That is right for a page (a caller
  that forgets shows fewer events, never more), but `feed-resolver-selftest.php`'s E22 asserted that a
  calendar-sourced event IS on the website, omitted the argument, and went red. The package had updated
  two other tests for exactly this and missed the third. Before changing what a defaulted parameter
  means, list every caller in `web/` AND `tools/`: here `grep -rn "MODE_WEBSITE" web/ tools/`.
- **A rule "judged on the organisation's calendar" cannot be tested in an organisation on UTC on a UTC
  machine.** Organisation 1 is seeded as UTC and the runners use UTC, so swapping `date()` for
  `gmdate()` in either public reader could not be seen. Section D of the test moves the organisation to
  Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14) from 10:00 UTC or Pacific/Pago_Pago (UTC-11) before it — neither has clock
  changes, and one of them is always on a different day from UTC — asserts that premise first, and
  plants `gmdate()` in each reader (P23, P24). #549's trap again: a fixture that cannot tell two zones
  apart proves nothing about which one the code uses.
- **Read a tick box by its VALUE, not by whether it arrived.** The handler first used
  `isset($_POST['showOnWebsite'])`, which is right for a bare checkbox but reads the common "hidden 0,
  then the box" pattern as ON when unticked. It passes the posted value to the judgement now, which
  refuses anything that is not a plain true or false.
- **Every place that says what "the public website" is must agree.** The form said "Nothing goes on the
  public website until this is ticked", while other new text defined the public website as including the
  search-engine markup on an event's page — which, for the portal's own events, follows "Public" alone
  (#850). The form, the help page and `api-spec.json` now all name what the switch governs today: the
  countdown and the sitemap. When the public door (P4) ships, it joins all three.

`check_event_visibility.py`'s `LINE_ALLOWLIST` is keyed by LINE NUMBER, so the slug probe in
`calendar/manage/save.php` moved three times in this package (537, 602, 607, 610); the check names a stale entry,
so it fails loudly rather than silently, but expect to move it whenever lines are added above it.

Round 4 of the check found the copied-in half leaking past the rule in two ways, both fixed in
`FeedResolver` and the choice page, and a lesson about reaching a refusal:

- **A box that "does nothing" on the website can still decide something elsewhere.** Under "one tick per
  event" the calendar's own website box was ignored by the countdown and the sitemap, but
  `FeedResolver::isWider()` still counted it as a yes already given, so ticking it made a choice's yes
  "not wider", applied it at once and released every date waiting for approval. `isWider()` now compares
  the yes that COUNTS under the rule, on BOTH sides, and `candidateAnswer()` STORES a yes only where it
  counts, so a rule's yes under the stricter rule neither waits for approval nor is stored. Under "one box
  per calendar" both are exactly what they were. Ask of any "inert" input: what ELSE reads it?
- **Change what a value COUNTS for, never the value itself.** Round 4's first fix set a rule's website yes
  to 0 where the rules' answer is formed, and round 5 of the check found that wrong twice: the rule preview
  compared the changed answer with the draft as written and called every matching event "another rule is
  stricter", and an approval is recorded against a fingerprint that includes the box, so an approval given
  under one rule was lost the moment the rule changed. The answer now stays as written; only the widening
  comparison and the stored value ask what counts.
- **Round 6 then found the fingerprint itself must count, too — and that the two directions need
  different answers.** With the box fingerprinted as written, an approval given under "one tick per
  event", while the approvals page said the box "does nothing", was reused to put the event on the
  website the moment the rule was loosened; and ticking that inert box sent every approved event back to
  waiting. `requestHash()` now records the yes AS IT COUNTS, so the inert box changes nothing and
  loosening asks again. Tightening would then lose an approval given with the yes counting, so the
  approval gate's step (c) lets an approval of the WIDER request (the same, with the yes counted) cover
  the narrower one; a decline of the wider one is not taken as a decline of the narrower. The cost, said
  plainly: after loosening, a date whose rule (with its website box TICKED) was approved under the stricter
  rule shows to its calendar's own audience until somebody approves it again.
- **"Until the next refresh" was untrue, so the rule's save now re-works every calendar at once**
  (`FeedAdmin::reworkCalendars()`, through `inFeedLock()`, the one place it resolves). A refresh that
  finds the outside file unchanged returns before the resolver runs, for up to `UNCHANGED_SKIP_HOURS`
  (20), so a switch could leave the old answer standing for about a day. Ask, of any sentence saying when
  something takes effect, what actually runs then.
- **Rounds 7 and 8 found the same machinery's edges, each by a case nobody had built:** step (c) must run
  whatever the box says (unticking an inert box lost a carried approval); pass 2, the sibling decision,
  must look for the wider approval too (a date added after tightening waited); only an APPROVAL of the
  wider request is carried, never a pending or declined one; and a newer approval of the wider request
  outranks an older decline of the narrower. Each has its own check and a plant that turns it red.
- **A form pre-filled for a GROUP of things must read the group, not one member and not a default.** The
  "every date" form, opened from a date with a choice of its own, was pre-ticked from that date (round 6:
  widened one date's tick to the series), then from nothing (round 7: narrowed the series off the
  website), then from the calendar's own box (round 8: ignored a rule holding the series off, so an
  untouched Save published every date with no approval), then from the series' other dates (round 9: a
  private or a stale date vetoed the tick). **Four rounds, four directions, so the inference was dropped**:
  a NEW choice asks "Show these dates on the public website?" as Yes / No with neither chosen, and an
  Everyone choice that does not answer it is refused. When repeated fixes to an inferred default keep
  failing in new directions, stop inferring and ask.
- **`settings-locks-selftest.php` (#836) ran nowhere** — in no workflow and not in the whole-suite runner —
  until 8 November. Its first run found this package's new lock missing from the add and delete paths.
  A test nobody runs guards nothing; `for f in tools/*-selftest.php; do grep -q "$(basename "$f")"
  tools/run-all-selftests.sh || echo "$f"; done` lists any others.
- **A form pre-filled from a stored value can turn an inert value into a live one.** The choice form copied
  `importWebsite` into its website box, so an untouched Save under the stricter rule converted a calendar's
  inert yes into a choice's live one. Pre-ticking "only a yes that counts" was tried next and failed too
  (rounds 6 to 9); a new choice now pre-ticks nothing (see above). **And a redraw is a pre-fill as well:**
  round 10 found the form redrawn after any OTHER refusal from the tidied post, where an unsent answer had
  already become "No" — so it showed "No" chosen. A redraw takes a question's answer from what was really
  sent, never from a value normalised for saving. Round 11 found that rule still incomplete in two shapes:
  a DISABLED control is not sent either, so "nothing sent" on a saved choice's box can mean "switched off,
  still ticked" — the redraw takes an unsent answer from the stored choice unless the box was live; and a
  form drawn as a NEW choice, redrawn after an unrelated refusal once somebody else had saved a choice, came
  back as that choice's form with its marker gone. **When a form's meaning depends on what it was drawn
  as, carry that in the form and refuse a save whose premise has changed**, rather than patching each
  path that loses it: a page drawn as new never saves over a choice that has appeared since. **And ask
  it again under the lock** (round 12, #647's rule): the page's own read is outside the calendar's lock,
  so two saves pressed together both passed it; `saveChoice()` now refuses `mustBeNew` over an existing
  choice inside the transaction that would write. **And refusing the save was not enough** (round 13):
  `saveChoice()` checks the form before it locks, so a post refused for another reason never reached that
  ask, and the page was then drawn as the newer choice's form. The page asks once more on the very read it
  is drawn from. Round 14 then found the half of that which matters — drawing the saved choice rather than
  what was typed — was pinned by nothing: a test of a refusal must also check what the page is redrawn AS.
- **A refusal no real account can reach is driven in a planted world.** In P1 every account that can open
  Manage Events may publish, so the handler's refusal is reachable only with the permission planted to say
  no (P25); without that, its `mayPublish()` call could be replaced by `true` with every check green.
- **A premise checked only when it is certain to hold is no premise.** Section D chose its zone so that the
  two days always differed at the moment of choosing; the real hazard was the clock moving during the
  requests, so the premise is now checked again afterwards.

### An own event's search-engine markup needs the website tick (D-089, #850)

- **The markup now asks the website rule itself.** `calendar/event.php` runs `EventVisibility::where()` in
  website mode for that one event, the rule the countdown and the sitemap use, instead of keeping its own
  test (`isPublic` for an own event; `importWebsite` plus `copiedTickCounts()` for a copied-in one). One rule
  means the page cannot drift from the two lists again. "Today" is `date('Y-m-d')`, because start-up sets
  PHP's zone to the organisation's, exactly as the countdown relies on. A copied-in event also needs full
  detail for the viewer; `redact()` near the top of the page has already emptied the description and place
  for anybody without it, so that test is a second guard.
- **This supersedes a sentence in the #493 P1 entry above**, which said an own event's markup "follows
  'Public' alone (#850)" and that the form, the help page and `api-spec.json` named only the countdown and
  the sitemap. True when written; all three now also name the search-engine markup. The event's page
  itself deliberately still follows "Public" (D-089).

### Readable colours from an organisation's own colour (D-091, #852 item 3)

- **Measure what the browser applies before believing a stylesheet's comment.** portal.css said the
  colour-mixed shades "shift the whole indigo family automatically". Measured in Edge: the dark half was
  overridden by a later block of equal weight with fixed indigo, AND dark mode's brighter main colour
  (`#7b86e8`) never applied for anybody, because header.php writes the colour onto `<html>` and a style on
  the element beats every stylesheet rule. Neither was visible from reading.
- **Contrast is a property of PAIRS, so a token needs to know what sits on it.** The fix is not "lighter in
  dark mode": white words on a lightened hover shade fail. `BrandColour` picks the words first (white
  where white reaches 4.5:1, else the design's near-black, else pure black — one of white and pure black
  always reaches about 4.58:1 on any single colour), then moves the hover and pressed shades AWAY from
  those words, so they can only read better.
- **A style block's selectors decide whether it wins, not only its position.** `html:root` and
  `html[data-bs-theme="dark"]` outweigh portal.css's `:root` and `[data-bs-theme="dark"]`; the browser
  test plants the block early with the plain selectors and goes red.
- **Count properties, not text matches.** A first count of "28 rules using the colour as text" was
  `grep "color: var(--portal-primary)"`, which also matches `border-color` and `background-color`; the
  real figure was 12 text colours plus two pagination tokens.
- **A fix aimed at a TOKEN misses every place that reaches the colour another way** (round 1 of the check).
  Links take the colour two ways: an ordinary `<a>` is painted from `--bs-link-color-rgb` (three numbers),
  while `.btn-link` and nav links read the hex `--bs-link-color`; neither was adjusted. And `.btn-link`
  and nav links' hover used the button's hover shade, which now moves away from dark words — lighter — so
  they got worse on hover (an ordinary `<a>` keeps its own colour on hover). Round 2 then found the
  three-number half was measured by no test at all. A
  selected outlined button and the `text-bg-primary` badge still sat on Bootstrap's own blue. None was
  visible to a test whose stand-in for Bootstrap did not model those values: the stand-in now does. The
  selected outlined button, the badge and an ordinary link's numbers each have a plant (P4, P5, P6); the
  `.btn-link` and nav links' hex colour and hover are measured by the browser test and guarded by PHP
  checks 4b and 4c, but have no plant of their own. Before saying "every use", list the uses by the PROPERTY that draws words.
- **`html:root` matches in dark mode too.** A light-mode value printed under it outweighs
  `[data-bs-theme="dark"]`, so the dark block has to restate anything it must keep (dark links).

### A new event starts members-only (D-079, migration 259)

- **A column's default is only one of the places a default lives.** `tblEvents.isPublic` started at 1,
  but so did three writers in code: the Manage Events form (ticked whenever the value was missing), the
  events API (a missing field meant true) and the CSV import (an empty cell meant public). Changing the
  column alone would have changed nothing a person does. Every writer is changed, and each has a plant in
  section N/P of `tools/public-website-tick-selftest.php`.
- **"Existing events keep what they have" is why the migration changes the column and runs no
  `UPDATE`.** An update would take public events off the signed-out pages without anybody choosing that.
  It is a `MODIFY COLUMN` restating the whole definition, not `ALTER COLUMN … SET DEFAULT`: SET DEFAULT
  left the old comment on an upgraded database, so it no longer matched a fresh install.
- **A writer can hide in an action that is not "create".** Approving a suggested event on the moderation
  page set `isPublic = 1`, so a suggestion became public with nobody ever seeing a "Public" choice; the
  first version of this package listed the submission form as already writing 0 and missed that Approve
  overwrote it. D-092 settled it: Approve leaves the value alone. When a default changes, search for every
  statement that WRITES the column, not only the ones that create the row.
- **No existing test relied on public-by-default** (the whole suite stayed green before section N was
  written), so the new checks are the only guard; that is why each writer has its own plant.

### A "not found" is not a failed request, and a check must read a page as a browser does (#821)

- **A 404 produces no `Network.loadingFailed` event** — the network part worked — so the only sign is a
  console line that names no address; the address is in the log entry's own `url` field, which
  `tools/layout-audit.mjs` used to throw away. That is how a missing `/favicon.ico` on `/api-docs` read as
  "a JavaScript error at 320px". The audit now prints it.
- **The browser asks for `/favicon.ico` once per run, not once per page** (it remembers the failure). To
  measure whether one page triggers it, audit that page alone in a fresh run.
- **Text that is present is not a tag that is live.** The first version of the new icon checks matched an
  icon link anywhere in the response, so the line commented out passed 34 of 34 (round 1 of the check
  planted it). They now remove comments FIRST (a comment may contain `</head>`), look only between
  `<head>` and `</head>`, and read `rel` as a list of words. The QR guard (#623) and the head-tags gate
  (#569) recorded the same shape. Parts A-F of the test still search the whole response; its header says so.

### The noticeboard's foyer screen (#493 P2b, migration 261)

- **`Portal\Core\NoticeboardFoyer` is the one place** that makes, replaces and checks the secret link,
  decides what the screen shows, lists its posters, and locks its two settings out of the general editor.
  In "public posters only" the list comes from `PublicWebsite::posterWhere()`, so the screen and the
  public website cannot disagree about which posters are public.
- **The organisation comes from the secret**, never from the address the request arrived at, and a
  switched-off organisation's link answers 404 (checks S7, plants P56 and P57). **That includes the
  Noticeboard's own on/off switch, and round 1 of the check found it did not:** `Router::dispatch()`
  tests an app's switch for the organisation the ADDRESS resolves to, and a signed-out screen always
  resolves to the default organisation — so a screen played on after its own organisation switched the
  Noticeboard off, and every screen stopped when the default organisation did. The route is now in
  `AppRegistry::ROUTES_JUDGING_THEIR_OWN_ORGANISATION`, which the router skips, and the page asks
  `AppRegistry::isEnabledForSite()` for the token's organisation (S11, plants P60 and P61). Any future
  page that takes its organisation from something other than the address needs the same two halves.
- **The parameter is `token` because the log scrubber knows that name.** `Logger::withoutJobToken()`
  blanks `key` and `token` before an address reaches the error log, an alert e-mail or the outside error
  service; the first version used `k`, so a fault on the screen would have recorded the secret (S12, P63).
- **The reload asks before it reloads.** A blind `location.reload()` that met the upgrade page, an error
  page or no connection left the screen there for good — and the portal closes for every release with a
  migration. It fetches its own address first and reloads only on a 200 or 404 carrying `X-Portal-Foyer: 1`,
  which only this page sends; otherwise it keeps playing and asks again a minute later. **The header is what
  round 2 added, and status alone is not enough:** the portal's service worker (`sw.js`, registered by
  `footer.php` on every ordinary page — not the login page, which draws its own — so on any screen whose
  browser was ever signed in) answers a page it cannot reach with the
  offline page and status 200, so a status-only check reloaded straight into it for good. **A status code
  says the request was answered, not who answered it.** **And round 3 found the worker could answer AS this
  page:** it keeps a copy of any signed-out page (it ignores `no-store` on purpose and refuses only
  `private`), and the copy carries the header, so an outage still reloaded the screen — from the copy, which
  also outlived a replaced link. The page now sends `Cache-Control: no-store, private` (S5, plant P65).
  Measured by the checker in headless Edge against the real `sw.js`. S13 reads the script as TEXT; no
  browser runs the real page.
- **The secret is in the address, so the page sends `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`**: a poster's picture
  may come from another website, which would otherwise be told the address. The page draws its own head,
  so it sends its own script rule too (#623) and is on `check_page_head_tags.py`'s exemption list.
- **The tiers follow D-086 and "the stricter wins":** `showsFor()` asks the installation first and
  answers "public" for anything it cannot read. The save is refused with the reason, never quietly
  changed (#668); the setup page asks `App::isSiteRootAdmin()` and `App::isRootAdmin()` for the two
  levels, as P1's rule card does.
- **What it cannot do:** nothing here proves a screen in a real browser plays the slides or reloads; the
  page's script was not driven (the HTTP test reads the markup, the headers and the script as text). A
  whole-database restore from before a link was replaced brings the old link back; the help page says so. P59 records that the token's shape
  test is a backstop: with it removed, a malformed secret is still refused because the lookup finds nothing.

### Noticeboard posters on the public website (#493 P2a, migration 260)

- **The board's editor cannot carry the tick.** The editor is a generated bundle (`dc-runtime`, not in this
  repository, #623). `api/noticeboard/save` replaces the whole board, but its `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`
  names only the columns it is given, so the three website columns survive every editor save and a poster
  it creates takes the column defaults (off). Plant P45 adds the switch to that UPDATE and section Q goes red.
- **A soft delete that keeps a flag can bring it back** (round 1 of the check). Deleting set only
  `isDeleted = 1`, and the upsert revives any poster whose id it is sent (`isDeleted=0`) — so an editor tab
  opened before the deletion put a ticked poster straight back on the public website with nobody ticking
  it, and it could not be unticked meanwhile because the page lists only undeleted posters. Deleting now
  also clears `showOnWebsite` (check Q7, plant P46). When a delete is soft, ask what each flag on the row
  means if the row comes back.
- **One judgement for events and posters.** `PublicWebsite::judgeEventFields()` and `judgePosterFields()`
  both call one private `judgeFields()`; only the noun in a refusal differs, so a poster can never be judged
  by a looser copy (#768's lesson).
- **The page asks the judgement on values read under a row lock inside the transaction that writes** (#647),
  so two people saving one poster cannot both be judged against the value from before the other's save.
